issue_context.title: networkctl does not show when configuration is loaded from Drop In
issue_context.body:
### Component

networkctl

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

When .network|.link configuration is extended with Drop-Ins, the configuration is honored and used as with other components of systemd. However `networkctl` shows the Network File and Link File without showing the Drop-In files when viewing status. 
```
# networkctl status 2
● 2: enp0s6
                     Link File: /usr/lib/systemd/network/99-default.link
                  Network File: /etc/systemd/network/00-enp0s6.network
                          Type: ether
                         State: routable (configured)
[...]

# cat /etc/systemd/network/00-enp0s6.network.d/routes.conf
[Route]
Destination=1.2.3.4
Gateway=192.168.64.20

# ip rou | grep static
1.2.3.4 via 192.168.64.20 dev enp0s6 proto static onlink

```

### Describe the solution you'd like

If `networkctl` reviled when Drop-In configuration was being used in a manner similar to what is done by `systemctl`, well that'd be just amazing!

```
# systemctl status sshd
● ssh.service - OpenBSD Secure Shell server
     Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/ssh.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
    Drop-In: /usr/lib/systemd/system/ssh.service.d
             └─always.conf
...
``` 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

250
comments: It would also be nice if some indication of the drop in configuration that is in use was also in `/run/systemd/netif/links/*` files too, but I think that's a requirement due to how `networkctl` works today.

review_comments: I prefer to show the dropins like `systemctl` does. I.e., with some decorations at the beginning of each dropin, in stead of adding the new entry for dropins.
I'm not sure how to make this work with the table helpers, systemctl does not use the table helper at all

How about to create a strv with `link` and `link_dropins`, whose first element is equivalent to `link`, and the subsequent elements are dropins with some decorations? Then, you can pass the strv with `TABLE_STRV`.

I'm not a big fan of "n/a" in such contexts. It can mean many different things depending on context, and it's also visually heavy. In particular, if there is no network file or dropins, we should just say "(none)". But this PR doesn't materially change this, so it's fine to leave for another time.
